pr_comments: I think likely this is fine since we don't have `type: module` on `worker_threads` but need to think for a bit since this means that we rely on the `-r` and `require.extensions` trick and `require.extensions` is deprecated. Since we support it in other places this seems fine at a glance though.

issue_context.title: Remove extension check on Workers since they can run with require extensions
comments: This sounds reasonable to me (the current workaround of just going through an intermediate file is fine but this is a reasonable ask)

I was going to open an issue, but I've found this one, and I think it's a similar scenario.

In my case, I was playing around with [ESM loaders](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#esm_loaders), everything works fine until you try to run a `.ts` file through a `Worker`.

I've made a demo https://github.com/macarie/esm-loader-worker; to run it use `node --experimental-loader ./loader.js ./index.js --file ./javascript.js` and `node --experimental-loader ./loader.js ./index.js --file ./typescript.ts`.
Both files, `javascript.js` and `typescript.ts`, import a TypeScript file, `fib.ts`, but only the first one runs. Using @CyriacBr's workaround, both of them work.

review_comments: Ummm, does this mean worker-script would run as CommonJS?
Yes, it will be loaded as a CJS module given current implementation.
